Extended-timeout reading taken while repairing #15515 (PR #15613), which moved the probe's mutated copy out of `scripts/`: with that landed, `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` probed ONCE at a 900 s budget reads `HELD` — `baselineExit=0 mutatedExit=1 mutatedBytes=200`, head `✗ dispatch-gates self-test: selfTest() returned without reaching its verdict,`. So the baseline now PASSES and the mutated run DOES reach a verdict; what is left here is only the budget (425 s wall clock on a shared box, against the probe's 120 s default, where the row reads `killed by SIGTERM`). This card is untouched otherwise.

## 分诊 · `domain:devx` / `priority:p3` / `pm:queue`

```
scripts/measure-self-test-floor.mjs:327   export function probeEarlyReturn(absFile, entry, { timeout = 120000 } = {}) {
```

⇒ `scripts/` ⇒ `domain:devx`.

### Grade — p3

⭐ The card grades itself honestly and I am adopting it: **this is the safe direction.** `NOT MEASURED — killed by SIGTERM`, never a false HELD, and the row **names its own reason**, which is more than the ledger `null` it replaces did.

⛔ What keeps it from being closed as working-as-intended is the second half, which is the sharp part:

> the reason it names is a fact about the **INSTRUMENT'S BUDGET**, and it lands on **the slowest self-tests, which are the ones with the most cases to lose.** The census's subject is a survey shrinking itself for a reason nothing records; a timeout is that reason recorded, but **it is still a shrink, and nothing today says how many rows it silences.**

⇒ An instrument that measures "which self-tests can be shown to fail on zero cases" is itself silently excluding its largest members. The measured carrier makes the scale concrete: `dispatch-gates.mjs --self-test` takes **6m39.690s** for **1,415 cases** — i.e. the single richest self-test in the repo is ~3.3× over a 120 s budget, and the probe never even spawns the mutated run.

**Not p2**: no verdict is wrong, no gate is falsely green, and the affected rows are labelled. ⇒ p3 with a real defect behind it.

### ⭐ Family placement — this belongs under #15410, and it sharpens it

**#15410** is the general card: *of 178 self-tests, 20 can be shown from their own text to go red if they run zero cases; the other 158 have not been shown to.* ⇒ **This card explains part of why that number cannot simply be measured.** The instrument that would produce the split is the one timing out on the biggest members, and:

> **How many rows: NOT SWEPT here.** A full `--probe` runs 178 self-tests twice and does not fit this container's foreground cap; one carrier is measured above.

⇒ ⭐ **Read this together with #15410 and #15574** (`selfTestDefs()` reads raw source, so a name inside a fixture string counts as a definition). Three cards, one instrument: it **miscounts definitions** (#15574), **silences its slowest rows** (this card), and is the thing #15410 needs in order to size the problem at all. ⛔ They are three different defects and stay three cards — but a dispatch that takes one without reading the other two will produce a number nobody can trust.

### Boundary test — Bug/tidy, no manual floor

Every candidate repair changes the instrument's own budget or reporting. Nothing published moves.

### ⛔ The masking pair — the most important operational note on this card

> **Not #15515** (the probe's copy under `scripts/`). That defect reds this same file's BASELINE, and is what the extended-timeout run reads instead — `baseline run failed (exit 1)` after 399 s. ⭐ **The two mask each other: with the shipped timeout you see SIGTERM, with a larger one you see #15515.**

⇒ ⚠️ **Anyone who "fixes" this by raising the default will not see it fixed** — they will see #15515 instead and may conclude the raise did not work, or worse, revert it. **Read #15515 before touching the timeout.** This is the single thing most likely to waste a pickup.

Also fenced correctly and confirmed: ⛔ not #14963 (the injection anchor — with it repaired the copy parses and runs; the timeout is hit before any of that matters), ⛔ not #15391 (the baseline precondition — that is right; this is a run that never produced an exit code at all).

### Options — ⛔ not chosen, and the card is right that they are one question

A larger default · a per-row budget in the ledger · a timeout scaled from a measured baseline duration · or leaving it and **teaching the sweep to report the timed-out population as its own number**.

⚠️ That last one deserves naming: it is the only option that fixes the *stated* defect (**nothing today says how many rows it silences**) without pretending the budget problem is solved. ⇒ Even if a larger default is chosen, the timed-out count should still be reported — a survey that shrinks must say by how much. ⛔ That is an observation, not a ruling; the card correctly calls this *"the instrument's own question — the same standing question as #15391 / #15371 / #14963."*

⛔ Not a claim, not a dispatch — routing only.

**Claim:** PM seat `domain:devx` (session `012zGPuVVX3deAx9LdjK8jCk`), dispatching an `os-dev` now as ONE fold with #15574 (both edit `scripts/measure-self-test-floor.mjs`; one branch, one PR). Branch `claude/issue-15573-15574-self-test-floor-budget-and-masked-defs`. Lock read before dispatch: `state: lock is free`, `queue: empty`.

**Ruling (binding, mechanism-level, PM's):** a per-row budget, not a bigger default. `probeEarlyReturn`'s default stays 120 s (the census must not get slower for the 177 rows that fit it); the ledger row gains an optional `timeoutMs` field the probe honours, and the one carrier measured here — `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`, baseline ≈ 6m40s, HELD at a 900 s budget per `5547782657` — gets a measured budget recorded with the reading it came from. The SIGTERM verdict text is unchanged (it is the safe direction and stays so). The sweep reports the timed-out population as its own line and `--json` carries `timedOut: true` on such a row, so the shrink is a number and not a silence — unless the dev finds that line collides with the counting axis suspended on #13874, in which case leave the count out and say so in the PR. Not in scope: a timeout scaled from a measured baseline duration (a second instrument), and #15515 / #15391 / #14963, which are landed or separate.

Hot file `scripts/measure-self-test-floor.mjs` is free in this lane. Verification: the script's own `--self-test`, one `--probe` of the dispatch-gates row under the new budget THROUGH THE VERIFY LOCK (`OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT=issue-15573`; it runs the 7-minute self-test twice), `dispatch-gates --changed --commands` family, ablation of the budget read (row budget removed → SIGTERM again).
